visa.name: B Permit (EU/EFTA Residence Permit)
visa.desc: No quota; proof of employment and sufficient language skills (B2). After 5 years, eligible for C permit.

visa.name: B Permit (Residence Permit via Quota)
visa.desc: Limited annual quota (~200 for nurses). Requires employer sponsorship, recognized diploma, and language proof (C1).

visa.name: L Permit (Short-term Residence)
visa.desc: For temporary contracts (<1 year). Available for EU/EFTA; third-country only if no local candidate.

qualifications.name: Swiss Nursing License (Berufsausübungsbewilligung)
qualifications.note: Required to practice; based on recognized diploma (EU/EFTA mutual recognition or third-country evaluation)

qualifications.name: Registration with Swiss Red Cross (SRK) or OdASanté
qualifications.note: Mandatory for professional register; language proficiency C1 required

qualifications.name: BLS/AED Certificate
qualifications.note: Often required by employers; valid 2 years

fit: Compassionate individuals who thrive in high-pressure clinical settings
People with strong interpersonal skills and multilingual abilities
Team players seeking stable employment with a meaningful impact
unfit: Those uncomfortable with blood, bodily fluids, or emotional distress

faqs.question: What is the average starting salary for nursing professionals in Switzerland?
faqs.answer: Entry-level nurses earn between CHF 60,000 and 75,000 per year, depending on canton and employer. Public hospitals typically pay on collective bargaining scales.

faqs.question: Can third-country nurses easily get a work permit for Switzerland?
faqs.answer: No – Switzerland imposes strict quotas (about 200 permits per year for nurses) and only admits candidates with recognized diplomas, C1 language skills, and an employer sponsor. EU/EFTA nurses face no quota.

visa.name: Residence permit for EU/EFTA nationals
visa.desc: Automatic for EU/EFTA citizens with a valid employment contract and sufficient qualifications.

visa.name: Short-term residence permit for EU/EFTA
visa.desc: For temporary contracts up to 12 months; renewable once for 24 months.

visa.name: Residence permit for non-EU/EFTA nationals
visa.desc: Subject to quotas; requires recognized degree, several years of experience, and a job offer with priority check.

qualifications.name: Swiss Federal Diploma in Computer Science
qualifications.issuer: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI)

qualifications.name: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
qualifications.issuer: ETH Zurich, EPFL, University of Zurich, etc.
qualifications.note: Common requirement for many developer roles.

fit: Analytical problem-solvers who enjoy coding and debugging.
Self-learners who keep up with new technologies.
Team players comfortable with agile methodologies.
unfit: Those preferring routine tasks without constant learning.
Individuals who dislike working under deadlines or pressure.

faqs.question: What is the average salary for a software developer in Switzerland?
faqs.answer: Salaries vary by experience and region. Entry-level developers earn around CHF 70,000-90,000, mid-level CHF 95,000-130,000, and senior developers CHF 130,000-180,000 annually.

faqs.question: Is it easy to get a work visa as a software developer in Switzerland?
faqs.answer: EU/EFTA citizens benefit from free movement. Non-EU/EFTA nationals face quotas and must meet strict criteria: a recognized degree, several years of experience, and a job offer approved by the cantonal labor market authorities.

visa.name: EU/EFTA Free Movement
visa.desc: EU/EFTA nationals can work in Switzerland without a visa, but must register for a residence permit (B or L) if staying >3 months.

visa.name: Residence Permit (B)
visa.desc: For EU/EFTA nationals with employment contracts >12 months. Automatically issued if criteria met.

visa.name: Short-Term Permit (L)
visa.desc: For EU/EFTA nationals with employment contracts <12 months.

visa.name: Third-Country National Quota
visa.desc: Non-EU/EFTA workers need a work permit subject to quotas and priority test; limited to managers/specialists.

qualifications.name: Federal VET Diploma (EFZ) Electrics Installer
qualifications.issuer: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI)

qualifications.name: Non-swiss Qualification Recognition
qualifications.issuer: Swiss Federal Institute for Vocational Education and Training (SERI)
qualifications.note: Required for foreign qualifications to work in Switzerland.

fit: Individuals who enjoy hands-on work and problem-solving.
People comfortable with heights and confined spaces.
Those interested in sustainable building technologies.
unfit: People who dislike working in varying weather conditions.
Individuals seeking an entirely desk-based career.

faqs.question: What is the typical starting salary for an electrician in Switzerland?
faqs.answer: Entry-level electricians earn between CHF 48,000 and CHF 58,000 per year, depending on canton and employer.

faqs.question: Can a non-EU/EFTA electrician easily move to Switzerland?
faqs.answer: No, third-country nationals face tight quotas and must prove specialized skills not available locally.

faqs.question: Is my foreign electrician qualification recognized in Switzerland?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must apply for recognition via SERI. Additional training or exams may be required.
